newsitem.title: USA: USDA's FAS says home page back up but no attaches.
newsitem.headline: USDA's FAS says home page back up but no attaches.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department's Foreign Agricultural Service reopened its Internet home page Wednesday after remedying a security breach but was not able to provide a popular feature, attache reports.

"That's one of the things we're still working on to get back on line," said an FAS official who asked not to be identified. She said FAS hoped to have the reports back on the web site in a couple of days.

The FAS shut down access to its home page on Tuesday after an unknown party broke into the system and began sending messages onto the internet. The site gets 20,000 "hits" a week from 6,000 different people, according to the FAS official.

Attache reports are filed by overseas personnel and provide assessments on crop conditions around the world. While not official data, they provide key information that goes into USDA's monthly world supply and demand forecasts.
